title: Why Waiting Feels Longer When Nothing Happens
short_teaser: Time can feel slower when we are uncomfortable, uncertain, or focused on the clock.
story: Time can feel slower when we are uncomfortable, uncertain, or focused on the clock. The same number of minutes may feel very different depending on attention and emotion. Our experience of time is shaped by context, which means changing the context can change the experience. Curiosity loosens assumptions. A better question can reveal options that certainty would have hidden. The lasting value is not merely knowing the fact. It is seeing the pattern beneath it and considering where that same pattern may already be present in ordinary life, creative work, or business.
impact: Our experience of time is shaped by context, which means changing the context can change the experience. Curiosity loosens assumptions. A better question can reveal options that certainty would have hidden.
spark_application: Take one assumption you have been treating as fixed and turn it into three open questions. Save a short note about what you noticed, what surprised you, or what you may want to revisit.
